The bug is in:

`org.joda.time.format.PeriodFormatterBuilder.FieldFormatter.printTo(java.lang.StringBuffer, org.joda.time.ReadablePeriod, java.util.Locale)`

Why:
- `ISOPeriodFormat.standard()` uses `appendSecondsWithOptionalMillis()`, so milliseconds-only periods are formatted through the combined seconds/millis printer.
- For `Period.millis(-8)`, `getFieldValue(...)` computes `valueLong = -8`.
- In `FieldFormatter.printTo(...)`, for seconds-with-millis fields:
  - `value = (int) (valueLong / 1000);`
  - with `valueLong = -8`, Java integer division yields `0`
- The sign is then printed from `value`, not from `valueLong`, so no `-` is emitted.
- Fractional millis are printed using:
  - `dp = (int) (Math.abs(valueLong) % 1000);`
  - which becomes `8`, so the output becomes `0.008`
- Final result: `"PT0.008S"` instead of expected `"PT-0.008S"`.

So the root cause is: negative fractional seconds in the range `(-1000, 0)` lose their sign because `printTo(...)` truncates total milliseconds to whole seconds before deciding whether to print `-`.

m26.content:
The bug is in:

`org.joda.time.format.PeriodFormatterBuilder.FieldFormatter.printTo(java.lang.StringBuffer, org.joda.time.ReadablePeriod, java.util.Locale)`

Why:
- `ISOPeriodFormat.standard()` uses `appendSecondsWithOptionalMillis()`, so milliseconds-only periods are formatted through the combined seconds/millis printer.
- For `Period.millis(-8)`, `getFieldValue(...)` computes `valueLong = -8`.
- In `FieldFormatter.printTo(...)`, for seconds-with-millis fields:
  - `value = (int) (valueLong / 1000);`
  - with `valueLong = -8`, Java integer division yields `0`
- The sign is then printed from `value`, not from `valueLong`, so no `-` is emitted.
- Fractional millis are printed using:
  - `dp = (int) (Math.abs(valueLong) % 1000);`
  - which becomes `8`, so the output becomes `0.008`
- Final result: `"PT0.008S"` instead of expected `"PT-0.008S"`.

So the root cause is: negative fractional seconds in the range `(-1000, 0)` lose their sign because `printTo(...)` truncates total milliseconds to whole seconds before deciding whether to print `-`.
